title: Ecology
tagline: The niche, life histories, population growth, competition, predation, communities, energy flow, nutrient cycles and biogeography
summary: Ecology studies how organisms interact with each other and with their environment, from single populations to the whole biosphere. This course covers the niche, life histories, population growth and regulation, competition, predation and parasitism, the structure and dynamics of communities, energy flow and nutrient cycling in ecosystems, and the large-scale patterns of biogeography.

chapters.title: Organisms and their environment
chapters.summary: Climate and physical conditions, resources, tolerance and the ecological niche.

chapters.title: Life histories
chapters.summary: Allocation and trade-offs, the timing of reproduction, r and K selection, and senescence.

chapters.title: Population growth and regulation
chapters.summary: Life tables, exponential and logistic growth, and density dependence.

chapters.title: Competition
chapters.summary: Intraspecific and interspecific competition, the Lotka–Volterra competition model and coexistence.

chapters.title: Predation, herbivory and parasitism
chapters.summary: Predator–prey cycles, functional responses, and the dynamics of hosts and parasites.

chapters.title: Communities
chapters.summary: Mutualism and other interactions, food webs, succession, and what controls the number of species in a community.

chapters.title: Energy flow in ecosystems
chapters.summary: Primary production, trophic levels and the efficiency of energy transfer.

chapters.title: Nutrient cycles
chapters.summary: Decomposition and the cycling of carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus through ecosystems.

chapters.title: Biogeography and macroecology
chapters.summary: Biomes, the latitudinal gradient in diversity, and the theory of island biogeography.
